title: Function Overloading
definition: Providing multiple function type signatures for the exact same function name, allowing it to accept different combinations of arguments and return different types based on those arguments.
simpleExplanation: Overloading is a multi-tool pocket knife. To the user, it is one single tool called 'Cut'. But if they pass it a piece of paper, it acts like scissors. If they pass it a piece of wood, it acts like a saw. The function signature changes based on what you give it.
realWorldExample: The DOM `document.createElement()` function. If you pass 'canvas', TS knows it returns an `HTMLCanvasElement`. If you pass 'div', it returns an `HTMLDivElement`.
useCases: Functions that can take either a single item or an array of items

basic: How many implementation bodies does an overloaded function have?
advanced: Why is function overloading in TS fundamentally different from overloading in Java/C#?

answers.question: How many implementation bodies?
answers.answer: Exactly ONE. You write multiple signatures at the top, but you only write ONE actual function body that contains logic to check the types of the arguments and handle them.

answers.question: How does it differ from Java/C#?
answers.answer: In Java, you literally write 3 completely separate functions with the same name. In TS, because JavaScript doesn't support multiple functions with the same name, you write 1 function body, and use TS solely to provide accurate intellisense hints to the developer.
